options.title: Select the note by title (any case) instead of by id.
options.title-optional: Select a note by title (any case). Without a note, the command covers the whole library.
options.format: Output format: tsv, csv or json.
options.fields: Fields to print: comma-separated names, or `all`.
options.nomod: Leave the note's modification date as it was.
options.limit-notes: Return at most this many notes. 0 prints nothing (use --count for the number).
options.section-write: Section address: a heading line such as `## Tasks`, or an address from `outline`. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.gate: Go ahead even if the write would drop attachments. Without it such a write is refused and the error names the files.

arguments.note-id: Id of the note. Give this or --title, not both.
arguments.note-id-optional: Id of a note. Without an id or title the command covers the whole library.

overview.summary: Read and write your notes from the command line.
subcommands: List notes, narrowed by location or one tag.
Find notes with the search query language.
Show a note's sections, each with its address.
Find a string inside one note.
Add text to a note or to one of its sections.
Replace, insert or delete exact text in a note.
Replace a note's text, or one section of it.
Send a note to the trash.
Send a note to the archive.
Bring a note back from the trash or archive.
Serve the library to MCP clients over stdio.

blocks.title: HELP
lines: theonotes -h, theonotes help       This overview.
theonotes help <subcommand>        Help for one command.
theonotes help all                 Every command's help in one document.
theonotes --generate-completion-script <shell>
Completion script for zsh, bash or fish.

blocks.title: OUTPUT
lines: --format tsv     Tab-separated rows without a header (default).
--format csv     RFC 4180 rows with a header.
--format json    One JSON document on stdout, errors included.
--fields a,b     Pick fields: comma-separated names, or `all`. The defaults depend on the command.
JSON shapes: a list of results is `[{...},{...}]` (empty: `[]`), a single result is `{...}`,
an error is `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}` on stdout.
Exceptions: cat gives `{"content":"..."}`, attachments save gives
Commands that change something print nothing on success and take no --format;
the exit status is the result. MCP tools return structured results for writes.

blocks.title: NOTE FIELDS
lines: id, title, locked, tags, length (UTF-8 bytes), created, modified, pins, location
(notes, trash or archive), todos (open tasks), done (checked tasks), attachments.
`content` is only printed when named, and `all` does not include it: use `--fields all,content`.

blocks.title: CONVENTIONS
lines: Exit status: 0 success, 1 the operation failed, 64 the command line is wrong.
Errors: plain text on stderr; with --format json a JSON object on stdout. The status is the same.
Tags: #one, #several words#, #parent/child. The leading # is optional on input.
Timestamps: ISO 8601 in UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).
Escapes: TSV cells and text options use \n \r \t \\. Text read from stdin is taken literally.
--content: read from stdin when the option is absent.
Notes are selected by id or by --title (any case).
Locked notes never give up their text through the CLI.

blocks.title: SECTION ADDRESSES
lines: A section is a heading and everything below it. Its address is the heading line as written,
`#` marks included; case matters, spacing does not. Several heading lines joined by `\n`
spell out a path from an outer heading to an inner one. A heading that occurs twice needs
its parents, or a last line holding a 1-based number that picks the Nth match. A last line
`preamble` means the text under a heading, before its first subheading. `theonotes outline`
lists every address of a note, and a wrong address is answered with candidates.
"## Usage"                the one section with that heading
"# Guide\n## Usage"       `## Usage` below `# Guide`
"# Guide\n## Usage\n2"    the second `## Usage` below `# Guide`
"## Usage\npreamble"      the text under `## Usage`, before its first subheading

blocks.title: MARKDOWN
lines: Notes are Markdown with these extras: ==highlight== (==🔴text== and 🔵 🟢 🟡 🟣 for colours),
~underline~, ~~strikethrough~~, #tags, [[Note Title]] and [[Note Title|label]] links,
$inline$ and $$block$$ math, - [ ] and - [x] tasks, pipe tables (a pipe at both ends of every row),
callouts (> [!NOTE], also TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION) and YAML front matter on the first line.
Switched off: setext headings, indented code blocks and lazy continuation. Long lines soft-wrap.

list.summary: List notes, narrowed by location or one tag.

options.--sort: Sort keys, comma-separated, each optionally :asc or :desc. Keys: pinned, modified, created, title.
options.--location: Which notes: notes, trash, archive or all.
options.--tag: Only notes with this tag or one of its nested children.
options.--count: Print only how many notes match.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: No match: `[]` on stdout with --format json, otherwise `No notes found.` on stderr. The status is 0 either way.
For negation, several tags or dates use `search`.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes list
theonotes list --tag work
theonotes list --tag work --sort modified:asc --fields id,title,modified
theonotes list -n 20 --format json --fields all
theonotes list --count

search.summary: Find notes with the search query language.

arguments.query-arg: The query (see SEARCH SYNTAX). A query that starts with a dash goes through --query.

options.--query: The query (see SEARCH SYNTAX). Use this form for queries that start with a dash.
options.--sort: Sort keys, comma-separated, each optionally :asc or :desc. Keys: pinned, modified, created, title.
options.--location: Which notes: notes, trash, archive or all.
options.--count: Print only how many notes match.

blocks.title: SEARCH SYNTAX
lines: words              all words must occur; `a or b` accepts either
"a phrase"         the exact phrase
-term              leave out notes that match the term or filter
#tag               the tag or its nested children; !#tag only that tag; #*/tag only nested children
@today @yesterday @last7days     modified then (any number of days for last)
@date(2026-10-26) @date(<2026-10-26) @date(>2026-10-26)     modified on, before, after
@ctoday @created7days @cdate(2026-10-26)     the same, by creation date
@todo @done @task  has open tasks / all tasks checked / has any task
@tagged @untagged  has at least one tag / has none
@title             words only match titles
@pinned            pinned in All Notes
@images @files @attachments @code     contains that kind of content
@locked @readonly @empty @untitled    note state
@wikilinks @backlinks     links to other notes / is linked from other notes
@ocr               also search text recognised in attachments
Filters combine: theonotes search "@today @todo meeting"

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: The `matches` field counts the text hits in each note; it is 0 for queries without words (such as @today).
No match: `[]` on stdout with --format json, otherwise `No notes found.` on stderr. The status is 0 either way.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes search "meeting notes"
theonotes search "@today @todo" --format json
theonotes search --query "- [ ]" --fields id,title,matches
theonotes search "@todo" --count

options.--section: Print one section: a heading line such as `## Tasks`, or an address from `outline`. Excludes --offset and --limit. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--offset: Start at this UTF-8 byte offset.
options.--limit: Upper bound on the UTF-8 bytes printed.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Plain output is the raw text with no escaping. --format csv: a `content` header and one quoted row.
--format json: `{"content":"..."}`. A whole-note read adds `"hash"`; a --section read adds `"section"`
(address, offset, length) and a `"hash"` of that section. `overwrite --base` takes such a hash,
and reading is the only way to get one. For metadata use `show`.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes cat <note-id>
theonotes cat --title "Mars"
theonotes cat <note-id> --section "## Setup"
theonotes cat <note-id> --offset 0 --limit 500

show.summary: Print a note's metadata as one row.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: A locked note shows its metadata, but asking for its content is refused.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes show <note-id>
theonotes show --title "Mars" --format json --fields all
theonotes show <note-id> --fields all,content

outline.summary: Show a note's sections, each with its address.

options.--section: List only this section and the ones below it: a heading line, or an address from an earlier outline. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: One row per heading and per section preamble, in document order. Every address can be passed to the
--section option of other commands; in TSV a multi-line address shows its line breaks as \n.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes outline <note-id>
theonotes outline --title "Cooking notes"
theonotes outline <note-id> --section "## Usage"
theonotes outline <note-id> --format json

search-in.summary: Find a string inside one note.

options.--string: Text to look for, ignoring case. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--context: Characters of context around each match in its snippet.
options.--limit: Return at most this many matches.
options.--section: Search only inside this section (a heading line or an address). Each hit names its section either way. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--count: Print only how many matches there are.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Each hit has a snippet and its section (blank in a note without headings). `source` is `body` for text in the note
or `attachment` for text recognised in an image or PDF; then `offset` points at the attachment's link.
Snippets use \n \r \t \\ escapes in TSV. No output with status 0 means no match.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes search-in <note-id> --string "TODO"
theonotes search-in --title "Mars" --string "water" --format json
theonotes search-in <note-id> --string "TODO" --count
theonotes search-in <note-id> --string "TODO" --section "## Tasks"

arguments.title: Title, written as a `#` heading above the content (below any front matter). Skipped when the content already starts with it. Without a title the first content line serves as the title.

options.--content: The note text; may open with YAML front matter. Read from stdin when absent. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--tags: Comma-separated tags to add. A leading # and whitespace are dropped; nested tags use slashes.
options.--if-not-exists: If a note with this title exists, return it instead of creating one. Needs a title.

--template.label: --template <template>
--template.text: Create the note from a template: the title or id of a note tagged #template.

blocks.title: NOTES
lines: --tags and #tags written in the content are independent and both apply. Prefer --tags: it puts them where
the tag-position setting says.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes create "My Note" --content "Body text"
theonotes create --content "# Quick Capture\nSome thoughts"
theonotes create "My Note" --tags "work,draft" --format json
printf "line1\nline2" | theonotes create "My Note" --fields id,length

append.summary: Add text to a note or to one of its sections.

options.--content: Text to add. It always ends on a line of its own, so it cannot run into what follows. Read from stdin when absent. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--position: beginning or end. Whole note: beginning is below the title and any leading tags, end is above any trailing tags and footnote definitions. With --section: beginning is right under the heading, end after the last nested subsection.
options.--section: Add to this section instead of the whole note (a heading line or an address from `outline`). Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes append <note-id> --content "New paragraph"
printf "New content" | theonotes append <note-id>
theonotes append --title "Mars" --content "Update" --position beginning
theonotes append <note-id> --section "## Tasks" --content "- [ ] New task"

edit.summary: Replace, insert or delete exact text in a note.

options.--section: Confine every --find to this section (a heading line or an address from `outline`). A find may span a heading inside it but not leave it. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--find: Exact text to look for. Repeat it, each with its own action, for a batch. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--replace: Text that takes the place of the match. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--insert-after: Text inserted right after the match. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--insert-before: Text inserted right before the match. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--all: Act on every match, not only the first.
options.--word: Match whole words only (Unicode word boundaries).

blocks.title: BATCHES
lines: Each --find takes the action that follows it on the command line (--replace, --insert-after,
--insert-before or --delete), so one call can mix actions. The batch is atomic: if one find fails,
nothing is written.

blocks.title: ATTACHMENT GATE
lines: A write that would drop attachments is refused unless you pass --force; the error lists the files.
Tag changes are not gated.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes edit <note-id> --find "TODO" --replace "DONE"
theonotes edit <note-id> --find "## Notes" --insert-after "\nNew line"
theonotes edit <note-id> --find "## Notes" --insert-before "Intro paragraph\n\n"
theonotes edit <note-id> --find "obsolete paragraph\n" --delete
theonotes edit <note-id> --find "cat" --replace "dog" --all --word
theonotes edit <note-id> --find "alpha" --replace "BETA" \
--find "draft note\n" --delete \
--find "## Notes" --insert-before "Intro\n\n"
theonotes edit <note-id> --section "## Tasks" --find "done" --replace "DONE"

overwrite.summary: Replace a note's text, or one section of it.

options.--content: The new text. Title and tags are derived from it (first heading, #hashtags), so include them. Links to existing attachments must stay or those attachments are dropped. Read from stdin when absent. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.
options.--base: Hash from an earlier read. The write is refused if the target changed since. Without it the write is unconditional. For a section write, the section's own hash or the hash of the whole note both work.
options.--section: Replace this section (heading and all that is nested under it); a heading line or an address from `outline`. The content must start with a heading of the same level. Empty content deletes the section. Interprets \n, \t, \r, \\.

blocks.title: NOTES
lines: The text replaces the whole note, so title and tags must be part of it. For a section, the heading line is replaced
too; to replace only the text under it, address `## Heading\npreamble`. A whole-note hash comes from
`theonotes cat --format json`, a section hash from `theonotes cat --section <address> --format json`.
The line break before the next heading is kept, so the content need not end in one.
A write that would drop attachments is refused unless you pass --force; tag changes are not gated.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes overwrite <note-id> --base abc1234 --content "# Title\nBody"
printf "# Title\nBody" | theonotes overwrite <note-id> --base abc1234
theonotes overwrite <note-id> --content "# Title\nBody"
theonotes overwrite <note-id> --content "# Title only" --force
theonotes overwrite <note-id> --section "## Tasks" --base def5678 \
--content "## Tasks\nRewritten body"

subcommands: List tags, library-wide or of one note.
Rename a tag across all notes.
Delete a tag from every note.

tags list.summary: List tags, library-wide or of one note.

options.--count: Print only how many tags there are.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Sorted alphabetically, e.g. `#several words#` and `#parent/child`.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes tags list
theonotes tags list <note-id>
theonotes tags list --title "Mars" --format json
theonotes tags list --count

arguments.note-id: Id of the note, then the tags to add.
arguments.tags: Tags to add. A leading # and whitespace are dropped; nested tags use slashes; names may contain spaces. Tags already present are skipped.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
Tags go where the tag-position setting says (bottom by default). The modification date is not changed.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes tags add <note-id> work "work/meetings"
theonotes tags add --title "Mars" favorite

arguments.note-id: Id of the note, then the tags to remove.
arguments.tags: Tags to remove. A leading # and whitespace are dropped. Tags the note does not have are skipped.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
The modification date is not changed.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes tags remove <note-id> draft wip
theonotes tags remove --title "Mars" draft

tags rename.summary: Rename a tag across all notes.

arguments.old: Tag to rename. A leading # and whitespace are dropped.
arguments.new: The new name. A leading # and whitespace are dropped.

options.--force: Merge when the new name already exists. Without it such a rename is refused, because a merge cannot be undone.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
Nested children follow the rename. A tag that does not exist is a no-op. Refused when the new name exists
(unless --force) and when any affected note is locked. Modification dates are not changed.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes tags rename work job
theonotes tags rename --from draft --to published
theonotes tags rename old-tag existing-tag --force

tags delete.summary: Delete a tag from every note.

arguments.tag: Tag to delete. A leading # and whitespace are dropped.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
Nested children are deleted with it. A tag that does not exist is a no-op. Refused when any affected note is
locked. Modification dates are not changed.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes tags delete draft
theonotes tags delete --name "work/old"

subcommands: Attach bytes read from stdin; a link is appended to the note.
Attach a file downloaded from an https URL; a link is appended.
Delete an attachment and its link.
Write an attachment's bytes to stdout.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: `size` is in bytes. No output means the note has no attachments.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes attachments list <note-id>
theonotes attachments list --title "Mars" --format json

attachments add.summary: Attach bytes read from stdin; a link is appended to the note.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: A Markdown link to the file is appended to the note. If the name is taken, a numbered variant is used
(`photo.jpg` becomes `photo 2.jpg`) and the link follows it.
Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: cat photo.jpg | theonotes attachments add <note-id> --filename photo.jpg
theonotes attachments add <note-id> --filename photo.jpg < photo.jpg

attachments add-url.summary: Attach a file downloaded from an https URL; a link is appended.

options.--filename: Name for the attachment. Defaults to the last path segment of the URL.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: The scheme must be https://; http://, file:// and data: are refused. A Markdown link to the file is appended;
if the name is taken, a numbered variant is used (`photo 2.jpg`) and the link follows it.
Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes attachments add-url <note-id> --url https://example.com/photo.jpg
theonotes attachments add-url <note-id> --url https://example.com/raw --filename photo.jpg

attachments delete.summary: Delete an attachment and its link.

options.--filename: Name of the attachment file to delete (required).

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: The file is deleted and its link is removed from the note text; no follow-up edit is needed.
Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes attachments delete <note-id> --filename photo.jpg

attachments save.summary: Write an attachment's bytes to stdout.

options.--filename: Name of the attachment file to write out (required).

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Raw bytes on stdout. Refused when stdout is a terminal, so redirect it. To get text, pipe through base64.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes attachments save <note-id> --filename photo.jpg > photo.jpg

theonotes pin remove --title "Mars" global work

trash.summary: Send a note to the trash.

blocks.title: RESULT

The note stays recoverable: `theonotes restore` brings it back.

theonotes trash --title "Old Note"

archive.summary: Send a note to the archive.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes archive <note-id>

restore.summary: Bring a note back from the trash or archive.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
A note that is already in the active list is left alone.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes restore <note-id>
theonotes restore --title "Recovered Draft"

subcommands: Show a note in the app.
Print what is selected in the note open in the app.

app open.summary: Show a note in the app.

options.--header: Heading inside the note to scroll to.
options.--edit: Put the caret in the editor. Ignored when a selection is set.
options.--new-window: Open the note in its own window.
options.--float: Show the note in a floating panel that stays above other windows.
options.--selection-text: Text to select once the note is open. Case-sensitive; it must occur exactly once. Excludes --selection-offset.
options.--selection-offset: UTF-8 byte offset where the selection starts. Excludes --selection-text.
options.--selection-length: Selection length in UTF-8 bytes; 0 or absent gives a caret. Used only with --selection-offset.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Prints nothing on success; the exit status tells the result. Failures go to stderr.
The app is brought to the front with the note open.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes app open <note-id>
theonotes app open --title "Mars" --header "Moons" --edit
theonotes app open --title "Mars" --selection-text "Phobos"
theonotes app open <note-id> --new-window

app get-selection.summary: Print what is selected in the note open in the app.

blocks.title: RESULT
lines: Both selection values count UTF-8 bytes; a caret is a selection of length 0. Empty output (TSV, CSV) or `{}`
(JSON) with status 0 means no note is open. A locked note reports its metadata but no selection or content.

blocks.title: EXAMPLES
lines: theonotes app get-selection
theonotes app get-selection --fields selectionOffset,selectionLength,selectionText
theonotes app get-selection --format json --fields all,content

mcp-server.summary: Serve the library to MCP clients over stdio.

options.--only-tags: Comma-separated tags. Serve only notes with one of these tags or a nested child.
options.--exclude-tags: Comma-separated tags. Hide notes with one of these tags or a nested child. Wins over --only-tags.

blocks.title: SETUP
lines: Point an MCP client at `theonotes mcp-server`. It speaks JSON-RPC 2.0, one JSON message per line on stdin and stdout.
The tools cover the same operations as the CLI, with deliberate differences: overwrite_note requires `baseHash`,
attachment removals are declared with `expectedRemovedAttachments` (the CLI has --force), and only the CLI has
--no-update-modified. Every tool carries readOnlyHint and destructiveHint annotations, so a client can ask the user
before a destructive call.

blocks.title: SCOPES
lines: --only-tags and --exclude-tags (or the variables below) confine the server to the notes those tags select.
Lists and searches show in-scope notes only, and a call that names a note outside the scope fails with `out_of_scope`.
With exactly one --only-tags value, create_note adds that tag itself; with several, the call must name one of them.
rename_tag and delete_tag refuse tags that define the scope. Use one server entry per scope in the client's config.

blocks.title: ADDITIONS
lines: create_note_from_template   An extra tool: creates a note from a template (the title or id of a note tagged #template).
capture_thought   An extra tool: saves the given text as a new note, unchanged.
THEONOTES_MCP_ONLY_TAGS     Same as --only-tags when the flag is absent.
THEONOTES_MCP_EXCLUDE_TAGS  Same as --exclude-tags when the flag is absent.

blocks.title: PRIVACY
lines: The server reads and writes the local library in place. It sends nothing over the network, except that
add_attachment_from_url downloads the URL it is given. There is no telemetry.
